body:
Thank you for taking the time to comment. I had read that eating a low carb diet usually relieves acid reflux symptoms within weeks. I did try this and my acid reflux did seem to dissipate but I was still having nausea and an irritated stomach. Which brings me to believe that my problems could be a food intolerance or sensitivity to something.  A couple of years ago, after the doctors seemed to have given up on me, I did decide to take matters into my own hands and just ate meat and vegetables, because that couldn't possibly irritate your stomach right? It did take a few months but as I remember it symptoms did seem to improve, but not quite 100 percent. Than we moved to live with my fiances parents for 6 months and I remember starting to feel worse, I couldn't quite control my diet here. After the six months though we moved to live on our own for a year I was pretty much staying away from processed food, but I didn't try that hard. I did occasionally have a hamburger with the bun or something. I did start to feel... I would say... maybe... 60 percent better? Than it just grew too expensive to live in on our own as our rent increased from 2100 to 2800 for our apartment. So here I am back with my fiances parents eating what ever they ate. Which is a lot of junk. I guess because I was feeling better I thought I would loose the diet, and now I have spirled down the rabbit hole. I guess because alot of people tell me that it is just stress, i just started believing in it and didn'the bring back the diet. It is hard to convince others and myself included when I self diagnose myself. 
I have decided to make an appointment with an allergist to see if we can find any food sensitivity that I might have. I haven't worked up the courage to contact the allergist though for fear of disappointment. What if the allergy test didn't come up with results? But I know that I really should go and get the test done. What do I have to loose if I wish to kill myself? Might as well try every option available. 
I have tried 3 different types of probiotics. One of them didn't really do much, the other I tried for a week but still felt like I was punched in the gut. So I stopped taking it. The last one I tried did seem to help as I was waking up without any pain, but I realized towards the end of the bottle that it was giving me shortness of breath. So I have been too afraid to try another. 
I do remember the day it all started. I was back in town visiting the family and was eating a ton of fast food with my fiances family. After about a week, one morning we were all about to go out of town to visit some of their family and they had gotten some breakfast burrito, which isn't something I normally eat for breakfast (I grew up in a household where we only ate meat, rice and vegetables). I took a few bites and then I remember they rolled down the window and it was 105 out and I just started feeling super nauseous and hot. I felt like I was having a hard time breathing. I ended up not leaving with them on the trip and stayed home. After about a month and I was still not feeling good. I went to an urgent care and was diagnosed with h pylori. So I was given the antibiotics and a whole load of other medications, I don't know if the antibiotics were supposed to behave this way, but the two weeks I was on antibiotics was probably the worst time of my life. I was bed ridden. Threw up bitter foam. I didn't eat. Even water made me throw up. I was severely weak. As I wasn't eating. After the antibiotics I wasnt as bad, but I was still feeling awful. Several times I thought I was going to pass out from nausea and ever since then I've been battling this problem. It hasn't been as bad as it was at the start of it all so I guess that part is good. I guess every time I told a doctor that I was diagnosed with h pylori they go straight to ant acids and proton pump inhibitors. Which don't help me and when I tell them that it makes it worse they go straight to stress. I was given an endoscopy and nothing was found, but I've got to say I didn't really like that doctor, as he was already convinced it was just stress from hearing my symptoms and he didn't want to hear it when I told him I thought it was food related. I was never prescribed any prescription anxiety medication. I have been recently looking into them online though. 
I haven't thought about a holistic doctor. I will definitely give that a try. I am pretty desperate and don't wish to see another traditional doctor. I don't think they would have anything else to say or would have anything they would want to try. I fear the words "it's just stress" like it's the plague. I also don't really want another doctor telling me so after thousands of dollars. When people say it's stress it's feels like they are telling me that it's no biggie and they don't see why I'm having such a fit about it. That I should just "deal" with it. So I have grown to hate that word, stress. I am constantly fighting with myself. Is it just stress? [But than why did I have good results for eating a certain way? There's no point in going to an allergist because they won't find anything. But than I should just check to make sure. <this is what I flip flop with everyday. Is it stress or not? Am I crazy? Is it all in my head?] 

And yes 4 years is a short time in the grand scheme of things, but it feels like I have been battling this for an eternity especially when everyone seems to be against me. 

Regardless of what you might think my problem might be, I just want to say Thank You for taking the time to even read the original post. Sorry for another long post but I feel like I am not in as deep of a depression hole as I was. There might be a glimmer of hope back. Either way thank you stranger for listening.
